---
title: "Installation"
---

## Stable release

::: {.callout-note}
The GFS dynamical core has been made into a seperate package called
[gfs_dynamical_core](https://github.com/Ai33L/gfs_dynamical_core) for
ease of maintenance.
:::

If you need the dynamical core, please install this package from source
or directly using pip. Doing this will automatically install climt as
well.

``` console
$ pip install gfs_dynamical_core
```

You can install climt by simply typing

``` console
$ pip install climt
```

This is the preferred method to install climt, as it will always install
the most recent stable release. On Ubuntu Linux, you might need to
prefix the above command with `sudo`. On Mac, it is recommended to use
the [anaconda](https://www.continuum.io/downloads) python distribution to
make installation simpler.

### What `pip install climt` installs

climt itself is pure Python. It brings in a companion package,
`climt-fortran`, which carries the Fortran-backed components (RRTMG
and the Fortran Emanuel convection scheme):

- on **Linux (x86-64)** and **macOS on Apple silicon (macOS 15 or
  newer)**, for CPython 3.10–3.12, `climt-fortran` is a compiled wheel
  and everything works;
- **everywhere else** it is an empty stub. Components that need Fortran
  raise a clear error when you try to use them; everything else works,
  including the CORK correlated-k radiation scheme.

To check at runtime:

``` python
import climt
climt.has_fortran_extensions()   # False with the stub
climt.list_components()
```

``` text
name                            kind                       available  requires  source
CorkLongwaveRadiation           TendencyComponent          True                 climt
EmanuelConvection               ImplicitTendencyComponent  True                 climt
RRTMGLongwave                   TendencyComponent          True                 climt
SimplePhysics                   Stepper                    True                 climt
...
climt-fortran: available, version 2.0.0
numba: installed
```

The `climt-fortran:` line says whether the companion is `available`,
`missing`, a `stub` without binaries, `broken` (with the reason it failed
to load) or an `interface_mismatch` with this version of climt.
`climt.show_versions()` reports the same reason on its
`fortran_extensions` line.

If an installed binary is faulty (for example it fails to load against
your NumPy), remove it with `pip uninstall climt-fortran`; climt keeps
working without the Fortran components. To build the binaries from
source instead (needs gfortran and a C compiler), replacing the stub or a
faulty binary:

``` console
$ pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps --no-binary climt-fortran climt-fortran
```

`--force-reinstall` is needed because pip otherwise considers the installed
stub or binary to satisfy the requirement and does nothing.

Some pure-Python components run much faster with numba, which is an
optional extra:

``` console
$ pip install "climt[numba]"
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Windows is not tested

climt no longer builds or tests Windows binaries. On Windows
`climt-fortran` installs as the empty stub, so climt installs without a
compiler but has no Fortran components. Building from source on Windows may still work but
is unsupported — if you need the compiled components there, the
[Windows Subsystem for Linux](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/)
is the recommended route.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
If you are not using Anaconda, please ensure you have the libpython
library installed. See the next section for instructions to install
libpython.
:::

Since by default pip attempts to install a binary wheel, you won't need
a compiler on your system.

If you don't have [pip](https://pip.pypa.io) installed, this [Python
installation
guide](http://docs.python-guide.org/en/latest/starting/installation/)
can guide you through the process.

## Installing from source

The sources for climt can be downloaded from the [Github
repo](https://github.com/climt/climt).

You can either clone the public repository:

``` console
$ git clone git://github.com/CliMT/climt
```

Or download the
[tarball](https://github.com/CliMT/climt/tarball/master):

``` console
$ curl  -OL https://github.com/CliMT/climt/tarball/master
```

Once you have a copy of the source, you can install it with:

``` console
$ pip install -r requirements_dev.txt
$ pip install ./fortran    # builds the Fortran components
$ pip install -e .
```

Until `climt-fortran` 2.0.0 is published on PyPI, `pip install ./fortran`
is required before `pip install -e .`, which otherwise fails because pip
cannot find a `climt-fortran` to satisfy climt's dependency. Without a
Fortran toolchain, install the stub instead:

``` console
$ CLIMT_FORTRAN_STUB=1 pip install ./fortran
```

Once `climt-fortran` is on PyPI you may skip this step and let pip install
the published package. These commands may require the use of `sudo`.

### Dependencies for source installations

climt depends on some easily installable libraries. For an installation
from source, it also requires that C and fortran compilers be installed.

On Ubuntu Linux, for example, these dependencies can be installed by:

``` console
$ sudo apt-get install gcc
$ sudo apt-get install gfortran
$ sudo apt-get install python-dev
$ sudo pip install -U numpy
```

use `pip3` and `python3-dev` if you use Python 3.

On Mac OSX, it is recommended that you use
[anaconda](https://www.continuum.io/downloads) as your python
distribution. This will eliminate the need to install numpy and
python-dev. Once you have anaconda installed, you will need to do the
following:

``` console
$ brew install gcc
$ export CC=gcc-x
$ export FC=gfortran-x
```

Where `gcc-x,gfortran-x` are the names of the C,Fortran compilers that
Homebrew installs. Exporting the name of the compiler is essential on
Mac since the default compiler that ships with Mac (called `gcc`, but is
actually a different compiler) cannot compile OpenMP programs, like the
dynamical core in climt.
